source.title: Are In-Context Images Worth 10 Dimensions?
source.authors: A. de Senneville; Xavier Bou; J. Anger; Rafael Grompone; Gabriele Facciolo

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends induction-head analysis to few-shot image classification in a large vision-language model and reports measurements of heads that attend to support-label tokens. It does not reproduce the original training-dynamics or circuit-composition measurements.
record.gate_note: The study defines induction heads by their attention to support-label tokens while predicting the query label, and reports head counts and head-accuracy results. It does not measure induction-head formation during model training, a training-loss bump, or the previous-token-head composition and token-copying mechanism. Other SDG and task results are not included unless they directly measure induction-head accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study's subject is the Shared Discriminative Geometry (SDG). It takes the induction circuit (Olsson et al.) as given, as the late-layer consumer of the SDG. Induction heads are picked as the top 5% of heads by attention to support-label tokens (following Cho et al.), so some always exist by construction. The head results (D.1.2) measure how far those heads depend on the SDG, not whether induction behaviour arises. Prefix-matching plus copying is never checked; only attention-based accuracy is reported, and only for Ministral 3 (3B). So no version is tested. The SDG-dependence finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. 'Induction heads increase after the SDG has formed' is a depth-wise result: the counts rise in layers just after ℓ*, not over training. The limitation about not directly identifying the theoretical circuit refers to the dimensionality-reduction circuit, not the induction circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures head-to-support-label attention and accuracy in multimodal few-shot classification, and tests SDG ablation; it does not reproduce the original induction-head training or token-copying analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Head counts vary by layer, with the reported increase just after ℓ*.

fits_no_version.finding: In Ministral 3 (3B) few-shot image classification, the heads attending most to support labels mostly rely on a ~10-dim SDG at ℓ*. Ablating it cuts the share above 80% head accuracy from 23.29% to 1.37%, and from 14.77% to 1.42% for all heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-like label-attending heads in LVLMs match query to supports through a low-dimensional shared representation built in earlier layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-5% label-attending heads cluster in layers just after the SDG peak layer ℓ*=16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-style label-retrieval heads sit in late layers, after the layers where example representations are formed (depth-wise, not training-time).

record.code_released: Code is included in the supplementary material and will be publicly released; URL not stated.
record.problems: Induction-head measurements are reported for only Ministral 3 (3B). The head-accuracy summary uses the share exceeding an 80% threshold, and the study does not directly identify the theoretical circuit in trained models.

untested.parts: No previous-token head composition and no [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying; the model is not a small attention-only transformer.
No training dynamics; the 'sudden increase after ℓ*' is across layers, not across training time.
No per-token loss and no attribution of in-context learning to induction heads.

Induction heads are defined by a top-5% attention selection, so their existence is assumed. Only one model (Ministral 3 3B) is analysed at head level; there is no prefix-matching/copying check and no comparison across families, sizes or runs.
Training data and setup are not varied for the LVLM.
Induction heads are not compared with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot learning. Table 2 ablates the SDG, not the heads.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 labels are dropped. 'Supports' rested on heads that exist by construction of the top-5% selection. 'Limits_scope' rested on an SDG-ablation effect and a one-model restriction; one-model coverage is untested, not limits_scope. A reviewer who reads D.1.2's baseline (23.29% of label-attending heads above 80% attention accuracy) as evidence of induction-style behaviour in a vision-language modality could argue for a weak T3 'supports' on V4. That reading would rest on attention only, in one model.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test composition with an earlier previous-token head or the [A][B] … [A] → [B] token-copying mechanism in small attention-only transformers.
No training-time formation window, in-context-learning gain over training, or training-loss bump is measured.
The study does not measure loss falling with token index in large transformers or whether induction heads account for most of that behavior.

Induction-head counts and head accuracies are reported for Ministral 3 (3B), not across multiple model families, sizes, or training runs. Other models are evaluated for SDG results, not induction-head behavior.
The study does not vary model training data or setup to measure effects on induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
It does not compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot task learning, or test whether other mechanisms carry most of that learning.
The study does not resolve training-time induction-head formation into multiple transitions.

conditions.value: across layers; increase reported just after ℓ*

rows.value: figure only; authors state that the count increases suddenly just after ℓ*
rows.note: This is a depth-wise pattern in a trained model, not a measurement of abrupt formation during training.
rows.check: This is a selection-derived value: heads are chosen as the top 5% by attention to label tokens, so the total count is fixed by construction. The plot only shows where in depth the selected heads sit, a layer-wise pattern in one trained model. It cannot show that induction heads exist in this modality, and it says nothing about formation during training (V2).
